patients.label: 70-year-old woman with AAST grade III pancreatic body injury and MPD disruption after a fall onto bicycle handlebars
attribution_limitations: The abstract states that EPS failed, whereas the main text describes an ENPD catheter that could not be advanced across the rupture; the source does not say that these are the same attempt, so they are recorded as separate procedures with unknown action.
The source does not state at which hospital or on which day the previous CT and the MRCP were performed, or the time of the first CT relative to the ERP.

Table 1 is titled preoperative and is not tied to a specific day; the text statement that amylase and lipase were elevated cites Table 1 but sits in a sentence about the next-day CT, so no day is assigned to the laboratory values.

The Figure 1 caption describes fluid collection around the stomach on CT (panel c), which the case text does not mention; the text cites Fig. 1b–e for the following-day CT, so the finding is linked to that CT only through the figure citation.

The source does not say whether the previous CT on which MPD disruption could not be identified is the enhanced CT from the other hospital, nor when the MRCP was done relative to transfer; the Figure 1 caption places the MRCP preoperatively only.
The source does not state when the ENPD catheter was changed to the EPS catheter; it is described after the POD 31 ERP but without its own time, so it is not dated to POD 31.

The laparotomy time comes from the opening sentence of the operative paragraph (Surgery was started 22 h after injury and 2 h after ERP), which scopes the single operation described; the gate flags it as borrowing because the sentence says surgery rather than laparotomy.

The source states the injury was treated and that pancreatic resection was prevented; these are authors conclusions from the POD 31 ERP and surgery, and no later follow-up after discharge on POD 56 is reported.

caption_claims.text: Preoperative MRCP and CT findings. From MRCP, MPD disruption was unidentified (a). The CT scan revealed pancreatic injury (b) and increase in fluid collection around the stomach (c), the pancreatic injury site, retroperitoneum (d), and pelvic cavity (e)

caption_claims.text: Preoperative endoscopic retrograde pancreatography and placement of an endoscopic nasopancreatic drainage catheter. Endoscopic retrograde pancreatography showed leakage of contrast medium (arrowhead) from the injured major pancreatic duct, and the pancreatic tail could not be visualized (a). A guidewire was passed across the break (arrowhead) to the distal pancreatic duct (b); however, the endoscopic nasopancreatic drainage (ENPD) catheter was not advanced across the rupture because the guidewire and catheter were warped (arrowhead) at the injury site (c). A 5-French ENPD catheter was placed at the injury site (arrowhead) preoperatively (d)

evidence.quote: Preoperative endoscopic retrograde pancreatography and placement of an endoscopic nasopancreatic drainage catheter.
